back: Rock formed when magma or lava cools and solidifies, e.g. granite, dolerite, basalt.
Rock formed from layers of sediment that are compacted and cemented, e.g. sandstone, shale, limestone, coal.
An existing rock changed by great heat and/or pressure without melting, e.g. gneiss, marble, quartzite, slate.
Slow cooling underground gives large crystals (granite); fast cooling at the surface gives small crystals (basalt).
Limestone → marble; sandstone → quartzite; shale → slate; granite → gneiss.
A long igneous intrusion (about 550 km long, a few km wide) running roughly NNE-SSW across Zimbabwe; chrome, platinum and nickel.
Younger sedimentary rocks (sandstone, shale, coal) in the Zambezi valley and south-east lowveld, e.g. the Hwange coalfield, plus basalt lavas (Victoria Falls).
Weathering and erosion → deposition → compaction and cementation (sedimentary) → heat and pressure (metamorphic) → melting → cooling (igneous).
Layers (beds) of sedimentary rock; singular stratum.
